22. I emphasise that we only provide this service to RFSICs. We do not provide this service to the general public. Hence, if a member of the general public or any building company that is not a RFSIC approaches us for an SDN application, we will not entertain such requests.

23. In other words, when a company approaches us for an SDN application, I would insist on a site inspection by myself or my staff. I will only proceed with an SDN application without a site inspection when the company approaching us is itself also a RFSIC.

24. It is in my view a sensible and reasonable arrangement for one RFSIC to assist another RFSIC in handling SDN applications, because many RFSICs either lack the necessary administrative manpower or simply prefer not to handle the administrative workload.

25. SDN applications can be burdensome for companies without dedicated administrative support. The process entails:

(a) Completing the required paperwork accurately, noting that providing inaccurate information is in itself an offence;
(b) Managing logistics, including tracking renewal deadlines and ensuring none are missed; and
(c) Liaising with the FSD, who may contact the RFSIC periodically to request updates on the progress of the application and the underlying work.

26. One example is PC&E. To the best of my knowledge, and based on my dealings with PC&E, it has only a few staff based in its office handling administrative tasks and paperwork (e.g. assistants and an accounting clerk), and the majority of the staff mostly work at work sites (e.g. foremen).

27. I honestly believed and still believe that this practice is lawful because:

(a) This is a sensible and reasonable arrangement;
(b) The actual works are still carried out by a RFSIC;
